subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: Should allowlisted POSIX shell-shaped gateway commands on macOS be eligible for no-prompt auto-execution when the current enforced renderer cannot safely rewrite the command?
rationale: The current behavior protects the exec security boundary by requiring explicit approval for commands whose shell expansion or wrapper payload cannot be pinned, but it conflicts with the documented `ask: on-miss` expectation and causes production approval floods.

options.title: Keep fail-closed, improve UX
options.body: Keep the current explicit-approval requirement for unenforceable shell-shaped commands, document the Darwin/POSIX command-shape limitation, and make the warning name the specific blocker such as tilde expansion or shell wrapper payload.

options.title: Add narrow enforceable support
options.body: Permit no-prompt auto-execution only for shell shapes the planner can rewrite to pinned executables and arguments, with regression tests and live macOS proof for each newly supported shape.

options.title: Relax allowlist matches broadly
options.body: Allow static allowlist matches to run even when the enforced renderer cannot pin the command, accepting a larger exec authorization risk for operator convenience.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed, improve UX
recommendation.body: Keep the current explicit-approval requirement for unenforceable shell-shaped commands, document the Darwin/POSIX command-shape limitation, and make the warning name the specific blocker such as tilde expansion or shell wrapper payload.

likelyOwner.reason: The current planner and one-shot policy for unenforceable gateway commands came through the merged planner work, making this the closest owner for the security-boundary choice.
